commonEvidence.test: all 34 workflow journeys persist through the real API with one domain-specific rejection each
commonEvidence.assertions: Each accepted command is reloaded and deep-equal to the response; every rejected command leaves persisted data unchanged. Journey ownership/counts and workspace isolation are asserted.

commonEvidence.test: workflow commands enforce patient, domain, request identity, strict metadata, and all version boundaries
commonEvidence.assertions: Rejects malformed/scope/version/forged metadata commands without a write.

commonEvidence.test: idempotent retries do not duplicate workflow history, audit, or downstream records
commonEvidence.assertions: Repeated exact commands preserve domain history, audit and projected records.

commonEvidence.test: anonymous and cross-origin requests cannot apply workflow commands or create private data
commonEvidence.assertions: Denies anonymous and cross-origin mutation before persistence under the test session boundary.

commonEvidence.test: legacy empty workflow snapshots migrate without losing existing chart data and can then save real commands
commonEvidence.assertions: Migrates empty workflow scaffolds while preserving prior patient data.

commonEvidence.test: corrections to partial reports retain original provenance and name the actual correcting clinician
commonEvidence.assertions: Original entries keep actor/time; later correction and note use the correcting clinician/time and the corrected report label.

commonEvidence.test: every journey maps to its imported workflow domain while preserving patient/program scope
commonEvidence.assertions: SSR/navigation mapping covers all journey IDs; missing or injected patient context is separately rejected. This does not execute interactive controls.

commonEvidence.test: malformed saved workflow slices fail reload without resetting or rewriting the stored row
commonEvidence.assertions: Invalid slice maps and nonzero slices missing state return 503 without modifying the exact stored row; restoring the row recovers all records.

commonEvidence.test: superseded signed plans are excluded from trusted coordination and decision references
commonEvidence.assertions: A signed amendment supersedes the original plan; old-plan support and decision signatures are rejected, while the current-plan equivalents persist.

commonEvidence.test: unprojected source workflow changes invalidate decision inputs until the source is reviewed again
commonEvidence.assertions: A preparation changes authoritative workflowInputRevision while legacy patient fields remain equal; stale/current-token-with-old-evidence saves are rejected and re-reviewed evidence is retained as a new revision.

commonEvidence.test: human handoffs project to one attributed queue row, preserve manual changes and close only with the source
commonEvidence.assertions: A handoff projects one source-linked queue row and contact task; repeat projection retains manual changes, later source transitions retain history, and source closure resolves the row.

commonEvidence.test: handoff without a due time stays in the queue and scheduling outreach stays explicitly unbooked
commonEvidence.assertions: A handoff without a due instant still projects to the review queue; scheduling outreach projects a due task while its appointment remains undefined.

commonEvidence.test: result follow-up task closes and reopens with explicit source transitions while notes stay versioned
commonEvidence.assertions: Result source transitions set the operational task completion state and preserve versioned notes.

commonEvidence.test: current signed plan follow-up supersedes a completed legacy plan task
commonEvidence.assertions: A completed legacy plan task does not mark the new signed plan follow-up complete; toggling the actual current-plan task does.

commonEvidence.test: partial observations show actual zero, unanswered and declined responses with their source provenance
commonEvidence.assertions: SSR shows 0 / 10 only for the actual zero response, missing/declined labels, original source, clinician and timestamps without mutating entries.

commonEvidence.test: correction chains retain original values and clinicians, with working links in both directions
commonEvidence.assertions: SSR retains both earlier values/clinicians, marks the current declined entry and verifies each correction link resolves to an existing element.

commonEvidence.test: numeric history uses saved sources and never substitutes obsolete corrected check-ins
commonEvidence.assertions: Numeric display uses the source of the active trajectory entry; absent matching source stays Source not recorded rather than using an obsolete corrected check-in.

journeys.title: Prepare the clinic and next visit
journeys.normalPath: Save a reviewed preparation, record new information, and review it again; reviewNeeded changes true then false and the latest information remains saved.
journeys.exceptionPath: An update using the preparation version from before the new information is rejected.

journeys.title: Enroll a new patient
journeys.normalPath: Enroll with reviewed baseline and consent/access readiness; retain declined video contact and an empty finalDiagnosis in a synthetic evaluation.
journeys.exceptionPath: Enrollment with consentReadiness=declined is rejected.

journeys.title: Reconcile missing or conflicting information
journeys.normalPath: Resolve an explicitly documented patient-versus-outside-list conflict and retain its previous unreviewed snapshot.
journeys.exceptionPath: Marking reconciliation resolved while its conflict outcome is still unreviewed is rejected.

journeys.title: Review treatment experience
journeys.normalPath: Save active treatment with duration zero, then a stopped report with duration unknown; partial benefit and side effects remain separate.
journeys.exceptionPath: Stopping without a stop reason is rejected.

journeys.title: Understand progress through the Digital Twin
journeys.normalPath: Capture synthetic observations with pain zero and a missing function baseline; pain is improved, function is insufficient-data, and provenance remains synthetic.
journeys.exceptionPath: A future receivedAt timestamp is rejected.

journeys.title: Compare options and patient priorities
journeys.normalPath: Capture discussion options, function weight 60, missing baseline information and evidence; defaultAction remains no-prescription.
journeys.exceptionPath: An option referencing evidence omitted from the captured evidence list is rejected.

journeys.title: Review PST and Shadow differences
journeys.normalPath: Store distinct synthetic PST and Shadow summaries, unsupported suitability and a request-clarification disposition.
journeys.exceptionPath: Claiming evidence-reviewed suitability without captured supporting or conflicting evidence is rejected.

journeys.title: Assess a new or unexplained problem
journeys.normalPath: Save a structured manual assessment and assert its completed status.
journeys.exceptionPath: The same finding cannot be both supporting and refuting evidence.

journeys.title: Support the patient between visits
journeys.normalPath: Link staff-recorded telephone support to the actual saved patient care plan/version, retain attribution, replay idempotently and save a revised summary.
journeys.exceptionPath: A wrong care-plan version and a stale support-record version are rejected.

journeys.title: Carry a concern through human resolution
journeys.normalPath: Advance a local high-priority concern through manually reported delivery, owner acceptance, review, documented action and response to closure; six transitions and manual provenance remain.
journeys.exceptionPath: Skipping delivery evidence or closing with failed patient contact is rejected.

journeys.title: Collect assessments and check-ins
journeys.normalPath: Confirm pain zero, unanswered function and declined sleep; explicitly correct function, retain all four original/corrected entries and preserve declined sleep.
journeys.exceptionPath: Ordinary save cannot replace an already confirmed observation report.

journeys.title: Reconcile external observations
journeys.normalPath: Save and replay a disabled, unconfigured source draft; adapter stays unconfigured and EHR launch remains not-validated. No live observation ingestion occurs.
journeys.exceptionPath: Enabling a live adapter or validating browser-claimed launch identity is rejected.
journeys.blockingReason: A separate local demonstration path is implemented and tested. Live provider/identity acceptance still requires configured external services.

demonstration.scope: Local dated report import, duplicate handling and quarantine resolution with retained originals.

journeys.title: Support language, accessibility, and caregivers
journeys.normalPath: Save unsupported-language/access needs, then an attributed manual Spanish translation; verifiedPatientAuth remains false and proxyStatus remains revoked.
journeys.exceptionPath: Self-asserted verified patient authentication and translated content without a reviewer are rejected.

journeys.title: Agree the plan and next actions
journeys.normalPath: Review and sign the saved assessment/observation snapshot; follow-up stays unbooked and delivery pending. Review and sign an amendment while preserving the original signed record.
journeys.exceptionPath: Signing an unreviewed draft is rejected.

journeys.title: Execute the care pathway
journeys.normalPath: Advance both operational pathway stages through active to completed, retaining five processed events.
journeys.exceptionPath: Starting a stage before its prerequisite or removing a completed stage is rejected.

journeys.title: Book and recover missed care
journeys.normalPath: Record follow-up due, request, manually reported booking, confirmation and retrospective attendance.
journeys.exceptionPath: Starting at attended, claiming booking without evidence or silently changing a confirmed appointment is rejected.

journeys.title: Review the episode and goals
journeys.normalPath: Review documented goals/outcomes and pending-work ownership, then close the episode.
journeys.exceptionPath: Closing an unreviewed episode is rejected.

journeys.title: Reconstruct a decision
journeys.normalPath: Sign the exact reviewed summary and distinct stored outputs against an existing patient plan; amend without changing the original; export exact patient/encounter-scoped JSON.
journeys.exceptionPath: Unreviewed displayed text, a fork from an already amended ancestor and a foreign-encounter export are rejected.

journeys.title: Launch from the EHR and confirm write-back
journeys.normalPath: Verify that accepted external event and bridge counts remain unchanged at the shared-owner boundary. Live EHR launch and write-back are not available.
journeys.exceptionPath: Browser ingestion and a forged server-adapter identity are rejected. The same domain fixture also rejects outbox preparation and acknowledgement without trusted server context.
journeys.blockingReason: A separate local demonstration path is implemented and tested. Live provider/identity acceptance still requires configured external services.

demonstration.scope: Curated patient/encounter launch, current-plan snapshot and local inbox delivery with failure/retry.

journeys.title: Recover interrupted or stale work
journeys.normalPath: Persist a draft, dispute and correct its actual summary, cancel and retry it, then re-review after a new source record revision; prior source records remain.
journeys.exceptionPath: Disputed/cancelled signing, a stale draft update and signing after the reviewed source changed are rejected.

journeys.title: Manage access, consent, and proxies
journeys.normalPath: Save a policy draft without changing the active policy and save attributed manual external evidence without changing the outbox.
journeys.exceptionPath: Policy activation, browser-asserted principal, untrusted write-back preparation/acknowledgement, unknown-patient evidence and stale domain versions are rejected.
journeys.blockingReason: A separate local demonstration path is implemented and tested. Live provider/identity acceptance still requires configured external services.

demonstration.scope: Patient-specific local consent and expiring proxy-access preview.

journeys.title: Configure the existing dashboard and program
journeys.normalPath: Draft, review and activate a documentation configuration drawn from enabled runtime capabilities; retain its original draft revision.
journeys.exceptionPath: Activation before review and rewriting an active configuration are rejected.

journeys.title: Author and publish a clinical pathway
journeys.normalPath: Document review and publication of a synthetic operational protocol; assign its exact published snapshot to the episode and retain it after a later draft edit.
journeys.exceptionPath: Publication before documented review is rejected.

journeys.title: Curate evidence and clinical content
journeys.normalPath: Create a dated synthetic evidence memo, request review and record approval in the local evidence registry.
journeys.exceptionPath: Approval before the review-request transition is rejected.

journeys.title: Govern model and software releases
journeys.normalPath: Record conditional release review, one rollout observation, one rollback observation and an approval with the exact configuration version; these are documentation records.
journeys.exceptionPath: Approval with unresolved conditions is rejected.

journeys.title: Operate securely and recover incidents
journeys.normalPath: Record, confirm, review and close a synthetic incident with closure evidence.
journeys.exceptionPath: Closure before review and reopening a closed incident through a draft rewrite are rejected.

journeys.title: Review monitoring-service documentation
journeys.normalPath: Save and review monitoring-service documentation while retaining the missing payer/legal review item.
journeys.exceptionPath: A duplicate with normalized case and whitespace is rejected.

journeys.title: Approve the exact release
journeys.normalPath: Record a proposed readiness decision with all mandatory gates; later evidence revision invalidates release/readiness decisions, preserves the prior proposal and can be withdrawn.
journeys.exceptionPath: Removing a mandatory gate during a proposed decision is rejected.

journeys.title: Track tests through result action
journeys.normalPath: Document requested, awaiting, received, reviewed, acted, communicated and closed result states. A corrected report reopens review, clears interpretation and retains the original before explicit re-review/closure.
journeys.exceptionPath: Premature result closure is rejected.

journeys.title: Close the specialist referral loop
journeys.normalPath: Document manual referral send/accept/schedule/consultation, retain original specialist advice, then review, reconcile and close.
journeys.exceptionPath: Closure before advice review and reconciliation is rejected.

journeys.title: Track medication authorization, access, and use
journeys.normalPath: Document medication consideration, clinician review, authorization, reported transmission/dispensing, reported start, response review and continuation; dispensing is explicitly distinct from starting.
journeys.exceptionPath: Skipping from considered directly to dispensing-reported is rejected.

journeys.title: Resolve access barriers
journeys.normalPath: Document a cost barrier, patient choice and an explicit resolution; retain the barrier type.
journeys.exceptionPath: A resolved state without resolution evidence is rejected.

journeys.title: Reconcile transitions and covering responsibility
journeys.normalPath: Document transition draft, pending ownership, reconciled instructions, patient communication and completion with explicit resolved pending work.
journeys.exceptionPath: Pending work cannot disappear when instructions are reconciled.

journeys.title: Coordinate multidisciplinary care
journeys.normalPath: Keep concurrent physical-therapy and occupational-therapy interventions, including the transport barrier, through explicit completion.
journeys.exceptionPath: Removing an existing intervention from the submitted list is rejected.

dependencies.production-identity: Production authentication, clinician roles, patient relationships, proxy authority and consent require the deployed identity/access integration. The API harness substitutes the verified-session boundary; shared-owner evaluation does not prove clinical authority.
dependencies.production-storage: API evidence uses real route handlers, prepared SQL, SQLite and reloads, with the PostgreSQL adapter substituted. Live PostgreSQL and deployed migration behavior are not exercised.
dependencies.clinical-validation: Synthetic workflow data and manually recorded clinical decisions do not validate diagnosis, treatment suitability, prediction performance, clinical safety or real patient outcomes.
dependencies.ehr-provider: Live EHR launch, source mapping, inbound events, trusted adapter identity and provider acknowledgements require configured external services; J12/J19 remain externally blocked.
dependencies.external-delivery: Phone calls, messages, referrals, appointment bookings, pharmacy milestones and handoffs are manually reported records. Tests do not deliver them or prove receipt by an external service.
dependencies.patient-access: Real patient/proxy authentication, interpreter/translation quality, accessibility usability and authorized audiences require separate evidence.
dependencies.prescribing-authority: The medication lifecycle records manual authorization evidence. No prescriber privilege, prescription, pharmacy transmission or dispensing service is provisioned or validated.
dependencies.governance-approval: Local review/publication/approval states are documentation only. Clinical, regulatory, security, partner-rights, payer/legal, production release and deployment approvals remain external gates.
